subject.title: Bound historical public repository proof reuse after expiry

question: What explicit expiry grace interval, if any, may historical public-repository proofs retain during simultaneous GitHub API and repository-page failures?
rationale: The report establishes the need for a bounded fallback, but the permitted authorization window is a maintainer-owned security policy decision rather than a purely mechanical implementation detail.

options.title: Use a narrow shared grace window
options.body: Adopt a small documented constant and enforce it identically in runtime and D1 checks, with boundary tests.

options.title: Disable expired historical reuse
options.body: Require `expires_at > now` even during historical fallback, accepting reduced cache availability for the strongest authorization boundary.

recommendation.title: Use a narrow shared grace window
recommendation.body: Adopt a small documented constant and enforce it identically in runtime and D1 checks, with boundary tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work covered the public-proof fallback surface implicated by this report.
